# Cyrus studios v2: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files: `item-designer.html`, `menu-quest.html` (tabs Menus / Quests), `mod-packs.html`, `import-mod.html`, `datapack-studio.html`. Self-contained, no network. Sources `src/` (v1 kit + `v2.css`/`ext.js`), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2, capped) into `shots/` (28 PNGs). Query params pick states; `ctl=0` hides the mockup bar.

## Principles
- **One product.** The shell copies the shipped studio (impl-shots/texture-*): the real portal sidebar and top bar, the Cyrus bar (wordmark, crumbs, context switch, Mod assets, token chip, theme), glass panels with mono eyebrows, the inspector tab anatomy, the conic-rim prompt dock at the bottom of the centre column.
- **One accent.** Violet means selected or primary. Cyan only means "now" (the simulator playhead). Green, amber, red only mean pass, warn, fail/blocking.
- **Typed, never node soup.** Graphs are columns (When, Only if, Do) with nested loop containers; blocks show their config path (`a0.n1`).
- **Caps are budgets.** Every limit is a meter or a counter (`20/64 actions`, `3/16 biomes`, `214/2048 progress chars`), and an overrun shows the validator's own code and message.
- **Honesty.** Real-client gameplay is "not verified" everywhere. "Not run" is never a pass. Sample content is labelled. The one illustrative Test Flight state is bannered as such. The attested scan never says safe.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data and caps |
|---|---|
| Item Designer | `ItemDesign` v1 (the Void Reaper fixture verbatim). Budget meters = `budgetOf()` ported 1:1 vs `BUDGET` (64/32/8/512/3), nodes 48, depth 3, 16 actions per list. Gate column = the `Ability` protocol (re-entry, cooldown, charges, conditions). Parameters = `params.ts` paths (`items.void_reaper.abilities.void_pull.a0.radius`) with `CAPS` ranges; saving shows "config.yml only, config_version 1→2, 27 Java files unchanged". Structure fields name the one Java file they rebuild. Simulator = `simulate.ts` semantics: charge = held/max, per-owner mark cap with oldest replaced, feedback text on cooldown. Asset chips run `canAsset` (texture top plan, sound Saka+). |
| Menus | `MenuDesign` chest (shop fixture: 6 rows, 28 list slots, 30 config entries, prev/next 48/50). Cost types item / xp_levels / economy; the CostCharger order room → pay → take → give drives "Try it". Checks use real codes (`economy_needs_vault`, `cost_loop`, `arbitrage_loop`, `slot_overlap`). |
| Quests | `QuestDesign` (trial_one/two/three, daily_bread fixtures): requires, branches (max 3), repeat daily, objectives with counts, rewards (max 8), stored-progress size from `progressEntryChars`. Backend is in progress (feature/cyrus-r11, uncommitted). |
| Mod Packs | Inventory (`scanServer`, redacted keys counted), findings with the engine's class/severity/resolution table, server-only findings separated, `notChecked` listed, `nxpack.json` summary (merged pack, `required: false`, changelog), compatibility row (static / boot, `not_run`), dynamic plan (1 combined + differential boots), the unit install steps and backup lifetime. Install off: `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL`. |
| Import | ImportDemo fixture: ingestion caps, build files read-not-run, attestation + share consent with the text-version ids, SPDX detection, the allowlist (placeholderapi, vault-api), `unsupported: X`, the attested profile's 5 real warnings, revision 0 facts from the node-2 run, token estimate from the reserve table (Saka standard 60–220). Jar = analysis only, dock disabled. |
| Data packs + worldgen | DataPackSpec v1 resource kinds and pack caps, six pinned versions, per-version emitted JSON (attributes + `#rrggbb` from 1.21.11, music list from 1.21.4, carvers map on 1.21.1), the function allowlist and refusals (live "Try a command"), function limits, the template layout spec (palette chars, `.` void, 48³, 32768 blocks, 16 loot containers), the cost heuristic and per-class recommendation, the restart / new-chunks banner. |

## Component inventory (React)
- Shared: `StudioShell` (existing), `DesignerSwitch`, `TargetVersionChip`, `BudgetMeter({label, used, cap})`, `IssueList({issues})`, `QualityPanel` (reuse).
- Item: `ItemHeader`, `AssetRefChip({kind, key, decision})`, `AbilityGraph({ability, selected})` → `TriggerBlock`, `GateChain`, `ActionBlock`, `LoopContainer`; `ParamField({path, value, cap, changed})`, `ParamsPanel`, `PendingEditBar({edits, files, configVersion})`, `DesignSimulator({design, events})`, `DisplayContextPreview` (reuse the shipped In game view), `DesignDock` (parameter-request preview).
- Menu: `SlotGrid({rows, slots, list, page, mode})`, `Slot`, `SlotInspector`, `ClickProtocol({steps})`, `ConfigListTable`. Quest: `QuestChain`, `QuestFlow` → `StepCard`, `ObjectiveRow`, `BranchColumns`, `RewardChips`; `QuestSimulator`.
- Packs: `MemberList`, `InventorySummary`, `FindingCard({finding, onResolve})`, `ManifestSummary`, `CompatRow`, `UnitInstallCard`.
- Import: `UploadKinds`, `IngestChecklist`, `AttestationForm`, `DetectedFacts`, `DependencyRow({state})`, `AttestedScan`, `RevisionZeroCard`.
- Data packs: `ResourceTree`, `VersionStatusRow`, `BiomeForm` (+ one form per kind), `EmittedJson({version})`, `TemplateEditor({layers, palette})`, `IsoPreview`, `FunctionSafety`, `WorldgenCost`, `RestartBanner`.

## Interaction details
- Graph and Parameters edit the same value; selecting a block highlights its settings; old values show struck through.
- Menus: Edit selects slots (numbers on hover); Try it buys with a sample inventory and shows each protocol step; arrows page the list.
- Quests: chain cards select a quest; player events advance the simulator; +24 h re-opens the daily.
- Packs: Apply / Acknowledge / Undo per finding; Install and Test Flight stay disabled while anything blocks.
- Data packs: the target version changes JSON and checks; paint template cells with a palette char; upper layers dim in the preview.
- Narrow (< 760 px): summary plus Approve / Reject on every screen.

## Accessibility
Kit focus rings; status always has text, not colour alone; `role="checkbox"`/`aria-checked`, `aria-required`; MC-coloured names sit on a dark chip in light mode; reduced motion stops the glint and dock rim. Open: keyboard painting for the slot grid and template cells, screen-reader summaries of the graph and the timeline.

## Deliberately excluded
Free-form wiring and code blocks (`run_command` does not exist), the dialogue-menu editor, forms for every resource kind (biome, template and functions are drawn), creatures/RigSpec, vanilla item art, prices, invented test results.

## Open questions for the owner
1. **Item icons.** The mockups use pixel icons drawn here. Production needs a source: our own icon set, or icons rendered from the client's assets (licence check)?
2. Should settings-only edits skip the model and cost 0 tokens (`planDesignEdit` is built, not wired)?
3. Menu and quest designers are still in progress on feature/cyrus-r11. Are dialogue menus and the 8-menu / 16-quest limits the scope you want?
4. Can a Mod Pack install while user-decision warnings are open (today: yes, unless acknowledgement is required)?
5. Third-party members: search Modrinth/Hangar, or paste a link? The download allow-list isn't wired.
6. Worldgen restart: automatic after install, or confirmed by the customer? On uninstall, keep or archive the dimension folders?
7. Are "Try it" and the quest simulator customer-facing, or creator-only?
8. Attestation and share-consent wording: approve the texts shown?
# Cyrus Texture and Sound Studios: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files: `texture-studio.html`, `sound-studio.html`, `mod-assets.html`, `locked-states.html` (self-contained; sources `src/`, build `tools/build.py`, shots `shots/`).

## Principles
- **Polish in place, no new look.** Tokens, type and chrome are copied from the v5 handoff (`app/dashboard/cyrus/studio.css`): deep space `#05030b`, glass panels, Inter + Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono, the TopBar crumbs, the conic-rim prompt dock, the inspector tab anatomy, the handoff's 1.7-stroke icon set. The asset entry is a new **Assets** tab in the existing inspector, over the network map.
- **One accent.** Violet is the only accent. Cyan only means "live": the playhead, the selected layer, the compare splitter. Green, amber and red only mean pass, warn and fail.
- **Truth first.** The mockups run the repo's real code (bundled from `lib/cyrus/textures` and `lib/cyrus/sound`). Quality panels show real `tq-1`/`sq-1` results (the Glock genuinely warns on `palette_size` 49; gunshots warn after peak limiting). Library rows are real manifest metadata. The only stand-in is library *audio* (it stays on the render host), and the page says so.
- **AI never overwrites**: every Cyrus edit is a candidate to compare, apply in part, or reject.
- **Real light mode**: white glass, inked colours; the portal rail stays a dark island, as in the portal.

## Mapping to backend data
| Screen | Data |
|---|---|
| Texture canvas, layers | `TextureSpec` (generated base, locked) + a raster Paint layer on top. Accepting a candidate swaps the spec. The PNG is a build artifact. |
| Palette, ramps | `spec.palette` (max 24, `MAX_PALETTE`). Ramps are UI groupings; "New ramp" generates 5 hue-shifted shades. |
| Style DNA | The prompt's CUSTOM TEXTURES rules (one outline colour, top-left light, 3-5 shade ramps, no noise or gradients, clear background); compliance is measured with the `noise` and `outline` checks. |
| Checks | `textureQuality()`: `transparency`, `palette_size`, `contrast`, `noise`, `outline`, `vanilla_lookalike` (`not_run`). `soundQuality()`: `format`, `true_peak`, `loudness`, `audible`, `silence_ratio`, `dc_offset`, `duration`, plus a subtitle row. |
| Sound events | `SoundSpec`: sets → events (`role`, `category`, required `subtitle`) → 1-4 weighted variants → up to 4 layers (`lib:` / `synth:` / `silence`, with gain, pitch, start, trim, fades) + processing. The key is `nx_<8>:<set>.<event>`. |
| Meters | `measure()` + `ROLE_PROFILE` bands; auto gain and peak limiting come from `renderVariant()`. |
| Pack status | R0/R1 sync states: hosted, delivery off (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL` off), unhosted; `required: false`; the Bedrock line from `assetLines`. |
| Locks | `canAsset(plan, kind, op)`, ported 1:1. Only create/edit is gated. The copy is the gate's own `reason` strings and the `downgradeSpecAssets` notice. |
| History | Asset revisions (spec + render + quality per revision). Restoring makes a new revision. |

## Component inventory (React)
- `StudioShell({studio, mod, plan})`: TopBar crumbs, Texture/Sound switch, token chip.
- `PixelCanvas({raster, zoom, grid, mirror, backdrop, tool, selection, compare})`, `ToolRail({tool, mirror, grid, color})`, `CompareBar({mode: split|onion|diff|after})`.
- `LayerList({layers, active, onToggle})`, `EditSteps({steps, at, onJump})`.
- `PaletteStrip({palette, ramps, color, usedCount})`, `RampGenerator({from})`, `StyleDnaStrip({rules, follows})`.
- `LivePreview({raster, mode: hotbar|hand|tile, bg})`.
- `CandidateCard({before, after, changes[], picks, qualityDelta, onAccept, onApplyPart, onApplyInSelection, onReject})`, shared by both studios.
- `QualityPanel({report})`, `CheckRow({id, status, value, limit, message})`.
- `EventList({sets, selected})`, `EventHeader({key, role, category, subtitle, onSubtitle})` (states: valid, missing).
- `VariantTabs({variants, candidate, weights})`, `WaveformEditor({pcm, layer, zoom, playhead, onTrim, onFade, onMove})`, `LayerLane({layer, solo, selected})`, `FxRow({processing})`.
- `LoudnessMeters({measure, role, gainDb, peakLimited})`, `LibraryBrowser({query, group, category, items})`, `SynthPicker({preset, params})`.
- `AssetsTab({mod, pack, textures, soundSets, plan})`, `PackStatusCard({state})`.
- `StudioLock({kind, decision})` (states: locked, plan_unknown, included), `PlanMatrix({plan})`, `DowngradeNotice({denials})`.

## Interaction details
- Texture tools: B, E, G, I, M, L, U; X = mirror, # = grid, +/- = zoom, Ctrl+wheel zooms, Esc clears the selection, Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift Z undo and redo. Every stroke is one step. Partial apply works per change (checkboxes) or inside the selection.
- Sound: Space plays, L loops. Drag a layer's edges to trim, its top corners to fade, its body to move it. Sliders re-render live. A/B plays V1, then the candidate.
- Quality checks re-run on every edit.
- Narrow: read-only preview, checks, play, approve/reject (approve saves a revision).

## Accessibility
Focus rings everywhere; tools have `aria-pressed` + shortcut hints; subtitle is `aria-required` with inline error; status is never colour alone; AA-tuned v5 inks; reduced motion respected. Open: the canvas and the waveform need keyboard pixel and handle movement (arrow keys + Enter) and screen-reader summaries.

## Deliberately not included
3D model or block preview (the "In hand" view is a flat extrusion), mob-skin UV editing (shown as "later"), animation and `.mcmeta`, reference-image-to-spec, image-model or AI-audio providers, spectrum view and pitch-preserving stretch, Texture Library contents (no source exists yet), prices.

## Open questions for the owner
1. Plan naming: the gate says Free / Katara / Saka / **All models** (Yakko); the handoff says Sokka/Yako. Which spelling is final?
2. Token cost per asset edit: the dock shows no estimate because there is no measured price yet. Should it show one, and when?
3. Should packs be optional on join (current default) or required?
4. Library licence: the bundle licence forbids redistributing the files. Do processed sounds inside customers' packs comply (legal check)?
5. Should the mob-skin row stay visible as "later", or be hidden until it's built?
6. Should mobile approvals be allowed, or should mobile be view-only?
7. Inspector width: Assets needs about 560px versus 480 today. Widen just this tab, or open the studios full-page?
# Cyrus Motion Studio v4: design notes (mockups, 2026-10-10)

Files (self-contained, no network): `motion.html` (a: motion panel + timeline + simulation controls in the studio shell; `?t=<tick>&tab=key|export|checks&row=<node.channel>`), `presets.html` (b: preset browser; `?kind=motion|effect|generator&sel=<id>&fit=1`). Sources `src/` (v3 kit + `mo.css`, `mo.js`), build `tools/build.py`, shots `tools/run-shots.sh` (node-2) -> `shots/` (dark, light, 390 px narrow). Plan: `MOTION-PLAN.md`.

## Real data, not drawings
Every frame, state, cue, log line, cap meter and "left out on Minecraft" row comes from the motion core (`scripts/cyrus/motion-mock-data.ts` in feature/cyrus-r21-motion): the gun state machine run with scripted inputs, the software preview renderer, `validateMotion` against Minecraft's motion capability and the Minecraft lowering's dropped list. The "What changed" list on the narrow approve view is illustrative.

## Principles
- Same shell as v2/v3: the studio switch gains **Motion** next to Texture / Sound / Model.
- One accent (violet) for selection and primary; cyan only for "now" (playhead, live state); amber/green/red for checks. The light-step lane uses the warn tone because it is a light level.
- Simulation and editing share one timeline: the machine row shows state bands over the run, tracks are drawn where they played, sound cues sit on a waveform lane (Sound Studio), scripted inputs tick the machine row.
- Per-game truth: the Export tab says what Minecraft approximates (segments, vanilla particles), what it leaves out (muzzle light), and that client smoothness is not verified.
- Narrow (390 px): read-only approve card for a motion; a compact preset list.

## Questions for the owner
1. Gating option A/B/C (MOTION-PLAN section 7).
2. Does Motion get its own studio tab (shown) or live inside Model Studio as a timeline mode?
3. Should the preset browser be part of the shared asset library (catalog kinds motion/effect) or stay a Motion-only view?
(Bash completed with no output)

# Cyrus build: what exists and what needs the owner (updated 2026-10-10)

Nothing below is deployed, merged to main, migrated in production, or switched on. All work is on branches, verified on node-2 / devhost.

## Branches and worktrees (chain; later branches contain earlier ones)
- `feature/cyrus-r0` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r0): version registry, launch-pair guard, starter-grant guard, reproducible jars, engine core (spec, revisions, namespaces, router, asset gate), Test Flight, pack delivery (pack host, managed plugins, Pack Loader), 26.x lane (inert), eval set (124 prompts).
- `feature/cyrus-r1` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r1): texture slice, sound slice (+ library manifest/taxonomy/search), texture library + unified catalog layer.

# Cyrus tracker: everything open, in one place
Last updated 2026-10-10 (evening). I keep this current; it is the first file to read after any restart.
Nothing below is deployed, migrated in production, merged to main or switched on. Everything is on branches, verified on node-2 / the dev host.

## 1. How Cyrus and Nxeon fit together (the separation, plainly)
There are TWO directions of traffic. They are different jobs.

**A. Cyrus needs things FROM Nxeon** (sign-in, who the user is, wallet/payments, listing a user's game servers, writing files to a server and restarting it, notifications, settings/flags, audit log).
- This is the **host seam** (`lib/cyrus/host`): small interfaces Cyrus calls. Inside Nxeon, one file (`host/nxeon.ts`) answers them with the existing Nxeon code, unchanged. Moving Cyrus out means giving it a different answer to the same interfaces (an HTTP client that calls Nxeon's API instead).
- DONE: settings, rate limit, audit, auth, permissions, users/jobs/servers/installs, database access (97 Nxeon-table call sites to 0), worker schedule entry point, host paths/config. A test blocks any NEW direct Nxeon import.
- LEFT (baseline: 40 import statements in 26 files): the mod builder library (28), Stripe (4), `lib/cyrus-mods` (3), permissions (1), 4 others. Billing and sign-in are decisions (below). The app routes/pages/components (185 files) also import Nxeon; those move with the UI.

**B. Nxeon needs things FROM Cyrus** (your idea: Cyrus is its own app and Nxeon feeds from its API: build status, a user's mods, the studios, library search, "install this mod").
- **Cyrus does NOT have its own external API today.** It has about 34 app routes inside the Nxeon app that its own screens use. There is no versioned, documented, token-authenticated API that another site could call.
- This is a separate piece of work I have NOT started: **Cyrus API v1**: an inventory of those routes turned into a versioned contract (OpenAPI), service-to-service auth plus user sign-in handoff (SSO), webhooks back to Nxeon (build finished, mod published, install result), and an Nxeon-side client. The Kodely partner pattern (SSO + Partner API, one account, one wallet) is the template; Cyrus would be the "partner" for direction A and expose an API for direction B.
- Recommended order: (1) finish seam A, (2) design Cyrus API v1 (a Sonnet audit + Opus design), (3) build the HTTP host adapter and the API, (4) run both modes side by side behind a flag, (5) move.

**Nothing breaks in the meantime:** inside Nxeon every host call delegates to the same code as before. Installs on customer servers, payments and your Nexion account work exactly as today.

**Move-day decisions (yours):** separate Stripe account vs Nxeon as the payment provider (wallet debits); SSO from Nxeon vs Cyrus's own accounts; new domain and cookie scope, and whether to keep `/mods/cyrus` SEO via redirects; where the Nxeon-side install API lives and how it authenticates; own database and Anthropic credentials vs shared. Top risks: Stripe customers/subscriptions live in Nxeon's account; balances must key off a stable subject id (never email); install records sit in Nxeon's `ServerMod`/`GameMod`; delivery uses SSH into customer VMs so an outside Cyrus needs a scoped Nxeon API, never credentials; hardcoded node-2 paths and credentials files (moved behind config, still to set).

## 2. State of the build (branches in /tank/dev-worktrees, integration branch `feature/cyrus-r2`)
Merged into r2 (1841+ tests pass, tsc clean): r0 foundation, r1 texture/sound slices, r2 conflict engine + Mod Packs, r3 import, r4 data packs, r5 studio UI part 1, r6 creatures, r7 item/ability designer, r8 worldgen, r9 Sound Studio UI, r10 item states, r11 menu/quest designers, r12 delivery + Test Flight gate + release record, r13 3D foundation (asset profile, glTF manifest + legal ledger, job queue + object store), r14 catalog v2, r15 host seam, r16 Model Studio viewport + paint, r17 cuboid/bone editor core + game-neutral timeline, r18 AI mesh service (meshgen), r19 playtest bots + Server Doctor + telemetry, r22 separation, r24 catalog scripts.
r21 Motion core MERGED (MotionSpec core, 9 presets, `motion` design kind, real flights 39/39 RCON on 1.21.11 + 26.2, sheets in motion-sheets/). r20 designers part 2 (boss/encounter + HUD/glyph) built and tested (1984 tests, real flights, scripted player 5/5) but merging into r2 conflicted with the motion kind in 17 files: the r20 agent is merging r2 into its branch; I merge after.
Running now: r23 Config and Stats Studio, Sonnet motion-assets pass 2, r20 conflict resolution, plus (launched 2026-10-10 night) r25 Cyrus API v1 (design + OpenAPI + thin read-only slice + HTTP host adapter skeleton), r26 asset library backend (storage, Postgres index design + fast search, contribution pipeline, takedown, Use-in-project), r27 designer studio UIs (item, menu/quest, boss, motion panel), r28 integration wiring audit + one consolidated deploy runbook.
Flags (all OFF): cyrus_studio_public_enabled + cyrus_tok_live (move together), cyrus_import_enabled, cyrus_studios_enabled, cyrus_model_studio_enabled, cyrus_model_editor_enabled, CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO, CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL, CYRUS_WORLDGEN, CYRUS_CREATURES, CYRUS_DESIGNER, CYRUS_ITEM_STATES, CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL, CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL, CYRUS_DELIVERY, CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE, CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL, CYRUS_MESHGEN, CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH, CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED, CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh, CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE.

## 3. Needs YOUR decision or action
**Review (blocks UI work):** v2 mockups (item designer, menu+quest, mod packs, import, data packs) in `cyrus-designs/v2/`, v3 Model Studio mockups in `cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/` (+ their question lists in DESIGN-NOTES.md).

**Open decisions:** (1) Stripe/SSO/domain/API/DB (section 1); (2) Config studio ungated? (recommended yes); (3) AI tagging: tier and cap (~133k input + 112k output tokens for ~27k leftover assets, likely cents; needs thumbnails first); (4) community library: does "usable by anyone" include "Use in project"; what happens to mods using a removed asset; real-weapon names hold vs flag; (5) paid eval run budget (124 prompts; start with ~30 textures) and real-client test day; (6) GPU / isolated worker for meshgen, template roadmap (which prop types first), pricing inputs; (7) Hytale: needs the Game Server Provider entitlement (each licence authenticates at most 100 servers); (8) handgun grip default sits ~2/16 block off the hand in third person: fixing changes shipped packs; (9) Mod Pack install with open warnings (recommend require acknowledgement); (10) attestation wording for import; (11) worldgen: restart automatic? keep dimension folders on uninstall?; (12) simulator customer-facing?; (13) item icon source for production designers.

**Legal (needs a lawyer):** Terms-of-service licence grant for automatic library contribution; telemetry privacy wording; Mojang EULA/marketplace and other platform AI policies (parked); content filters (trademark list is a stub).

## 4. Assets (staging only: /tank/cyrus-library-staging, not git, not served)
- 62,095 rows staged (CC0): 10,278 models, 2,946 PBR sets, 1,430 HDRIs, 38,464 Kenney sprites (inflated), 2,752 textures, 127 decals, ~6,000 sounds incl. your 2,964-file proprietary SFX library.
- Catalog v2 free stage (no AI): 60,970 entries, 55.3% fully described; audio measured for 6,088 sounds. Entries in `catalog-v2/`.
- Excluded (kept aside): 4,132 CC-BY rows; Quaternius Bestiary (new no-redistribution licence); Mixamo/CMU.
- Still to do: your nested "Minecraft GFX and SFX.zip" not opened; 10 sounds failed to decode; Smithsonian 199 of 2,326 verified models staged (`tools/si2.py` resumes); FSD50K downloading slowly (keep CC0 half only); NASA models and Warfork sounds need your call; thumbnails for ~18k assets (script, free) before any AI tagging; per-pack licence documents for the proprietary library before clearing it; numeric pack folder names (1-10) carry no description.
- Motion/effects: 1,972 rows (animation clips, flipbooks, particle textures); gaps (water, doors, effect presets) are being authored: Sonnet pass 2 (FBX to glb, 150+ procedural flipbooks) and Motion core presets.
- Catalog gaps: search index (SQLite) too slow for broad queries (17 s; memory index 0.06-0.65 s); no Postgres backend or browse UI yet; trademark/real-weapon/NSFW filters are stubs; effect/motion vocabulary proposed but not in the repo.

## 5. Gaps and unverified (be honest about these)
- **No real Minecraft client has loaded a pack, texture, sound or model.** The (T) items in the plan are all unverified in a real client.
- **No paid model build has run** for texture/sound/datapack/import/designer/meshgen specs: AI output quality is unverified; token costs are estimates.
- Designer in-game behaviour (clicks, projectiles, loot, menus, quests) verified by RCON/log on 1.21.11 and 26.2 only; other versions have no javac classpath.
- Playtest bots verified on 1.21.11 only. Server Doctor tested on a throwaway server only. Telemetry is schema + unit tests.
- Creature paint compile into the delivered skin not built; creature look/animation unverified (BetterModel limits undocumented); Model Studio layer 1 UI follows unreviewed mockups; editor 3D area still a stand-in until wired to the viewport; editor saves are overwritten by the next build and there is no server draft table for the editor.
- Hytale: `.blockyanim` schema, texture limits, server/auth details unverified (official pages 403); exporter is a draft at maturity "planned". FiveM natives unverified.
- meshgen: no real model call, LODs, in-engine load, kernel-escape test, or isolated worker; drum magazine looks like a wheel; parts overlap rather than union.
- Test Flight: one flight at a time, no container limits; worldgen rollback proven in tests and one real flight; creature hand-off with real BetterModel unrun.
- Minecraft versions: 26.3 has no stable Paper build; 1.21.1 needs a legacy item-model emitter (not built).
- Known flake: `cyrus-admin.test.ts` fails only in the big parallel batch (passes alone).

I'll port this as a pixel-icons design file acting as placeholder icons, flagging it as an open question. I'm wondering whether design items with a matching texture could instead render the real TextureDoc from studio assets client-side, using the Texture Studio's rendering pipeline when the project's texture key matches the design's model key.

That seems feasible by fetching the studio assets view, gated behind the same viewer permission as the designers tab—real textures where available, placeholder pixel art for vanilla items feels like a nice honest touch. I'll keep this in scope but simple, checking later whether the rendering function is client-safe.

Now I want to move on to the motion mockups and the r20 boss spec before planning the architecture; to manage scope I'll tackle screens 1 and 2 fully first, then 3 and 4, starting with the motion shots since they affect whether the studio switcher shell includes designers.

The Motion panel looks substantial with its 3D preview and timeline — there's already a Model Studio with an r17 timeline editor and a software rasterizer for motion previews I might be able to reuse. I'll tackle this after the first few items, and should check the motion design kind spec and related lib files.

Now I'm sketching the backend architecture for screens 1-2 under a new `lib/cyrus/designer/studio/` folder: a `service.ts` with injected dependencies (store, chain, drafts) exposing a `designsView` function that resolves the project's design rows, validates them against gameplay rules for the chain version and namespace, and returns designs plus per-file issues, budgets, params, revision info, and compiled summaries. I'm also planning a `checkDesigns` function that validates an unsaved working copy and returns the same validation, budgets, and diff against the saved version without writing anything.

I'm outlining additional pieces: a `simulate` function running the DesignSimulator or GameplaySimulator for scenario testing, and a `saveDesigns` function that validates, compiles, diffs against the prior save, then records a new revision and asset entry with provenance metadata, checking for stale heads. For drafts, I'm deciding to store one working-copy document per project keyed under "designer" rather than per individual design, since saves are mod-wide. Then I'm sketching `http.ts` as framework-free handlers for viewing, checking, simulating, saving revisions, and managing drafts, gated by studio visibility plus a designer feature flag.

Thinking through the gating logic, I conclude both the studios viewer check and the CYRUS_DESIGNER env flag need to pass together, failing closed by default since without the flag no designs exist regardless. I'm also laying out the real dependency wiring using studios services and draft storage, plus the concrete API routes (projects, check, simulate, revisions, draft) and dashboard pages for items, menus/quests, and bosses tabs.

Designers aren't plan-gated themselves, but asset edits follow the existing asset permission checks for textures and sounds, determining whether the "open in studio" action shows or gets locked behind a plan upgrade. I'm also working through token costs on the dock: parameter-only edits should apply deterministically with zero model calls and no tokens, while structural changes require an estimated token range, though exactly how Send behaves for config-only edits still needs to be wired.

For param edits, I'll add a lightweight plan endpoint that parses the edit request and applies it locally without billing implications, since it's equivalent to the user typing values directly. For structural requests, since there's no designer candidate backend yet, I'll avoid triggering paid change builds and instead just surface the token estimate alongside a disabled or "open in" action.

For structural requests, I'm thinking of a simpler honest approach: a "Send as a change build" button that links to the mod's main page change-request flow with the text prefilled and the token estimate shown via the existing estimate component, rather than building a new backend path.

For the simulator, I'm sketching mockup controls like hit next mob, hit a cow, charge-and-release timing, and reset, backed by a server endpoint that takes the designs, item, and a generic script of events (hit, charge, wait), runs it through a fresh DesignSimulator against a sample world, and returns a log plus timeline bars showing charge/cooldown intervals and mark counts.

The client should hold onto the script list and deterministically re-simulate on every button press, and the available buttons should be derived generically from the item's trigger types -- things like hit-next-mob/hit-a-cow for left_click_hit_entity, kill-next-mob for kill_entity, right-click and sneak-right-click variants, charge-and-release controls, hold-duration for held_interval, consume, join/die, and projectile-hit, plus always-available time-advance and reset buttons. I'm also setting up a simple sample world with the player positioned at the origin facing a direction.

I need to look at how the simulator actually handles events, so I'm reading lines 300-397 of simulate.ts to understand the mob positions and event construction logic before building this out properly.

I need to figure out whether the designer should support saving structural edits that recompile the whole mod, or restrict editing to safe parameter adjustments only.

Since save operations go through the service rather than being delivered live, structural edits could be saved as revisions labeled to indicate they'll trigger a rebuild of certain Java files on the next build. For the "+ Action" and "+ Condition" buttons, I'll scope it down to simple add/remove functionality for actions and conditions rather than a complete type picker.

I'll offer a short menu of common action types with sensible defaults (particles, sound, message, actionbar, potion, heal, damage) and support deleting any selected block, with structural fields like particle type, color, and target shown as chips carrying a tooltip noting they trigger a rebuild, while remaining editable in the JSON view. With the backend done, I'm shifting to the UI, planning out the designer components: an API client file for fetching designer data, a CSS stylesheet porting the v2 mockup styles with a cys/dz prefix convention, and a placeholder icon set file.

I'm sketching the shared component layer: a DesignerShell wrapping StudioShell with a switch between Items/Menus/Quests/Bosses, plus supporting pieces like BudgetMeter, IssueList, Stepper, PendingBar, a useDesigner hook handling load/autosave/debounced checks, and smaller helpers like McText and ItemIcon. Then individual designer files for Items, MenuQuest, and Bosses, plus hooking motion into the studio shell.

For StudioShell, I need to extend it so the right-side switcher (currently Texture/Sound/Model) can be swapped for an Items/Menus/Quests segment — adding optional `seg` and `icon` props to keep the change minimal, along with a data-studio attribute. I'm also starting to map out the corresponding dashboard page routes.

Now I'm working through the page routes for items, menus (with quests tab), and bosses, each gated by requireModBuilderUser and designerStudioOn checks, plus the useDesigner hook's internal state — tracking the server view, working file copy, debounced analysis, checking flag, and saved state, with edit/save/discard actions and autosave logic. I'm also figuring out draft restoration behavior: auto-restoring unsaved edits with a banner showing the restore time, and warning the user if the mod has changed since the draft was made, blocking save until they discard or reload.

For the stale draft case, I decide it's too risky to auto-apply since it could silently overwrite newer changes with outdated values, so I'll skip auto-restore and just show a "Discard draft" banner instead. Then I'm sketching the item designer's three-column layout: a left sidebar with lists for designs, abilities, marks, assets, and the recipe grid, and a center panel with the item header (icon, name, rarity, lore, stats) and an ability graph panel.

Within the ability graph panel I'm detailing a header row with name, error count, node/depth stats, and a Graph/JSON toggle, plus budget meters and a When/Only if/Do column layout, ending with a footer and dock hint. On the right side I'm laying out the live preview with a texture-based canvas, parameter/simulator/checks tabs, and a pending-changes bar, while also considering phone-narrow and light-mode styling, plus how structural asset edits trigger a token-cost estimate and apply through the design-edit planning flow.

For a model-driven structural change, I'm noting we shouldn't kick off builds directly from this view — instead show a note that structure changes route through a change build, with a link into Cyrus pointing at the build page with a prefill parameter. content.content:
# Cyrus Motion Core: architecture (v4, 2026-10-10)

Owner decision: motion, animation and effects are FOUNDATIONAL and game-neutral. One data model describes a creature walk, a gun cock/fire/reload, a door on a hinge, an explosion, fire, smoke or a splash, and (later, not on Minecraft) a vehicle with wheels, doors, seats and a character getting in. Per-game details live only in adapters. Research and labels: `cyrus-research/R-motion-effects.md` (V = verified, U = unverified). Code: `lib/cyrus/motion/` (pure core) and `lib/cyrus/designer/motion/` (Minecraft lowering as a designer kind).

## 1. Data model: MotionSpec v1

```
MotionSpec { schemaVersion: 1, id, title?, rig: { nodes[] }, clips[], machines[], meta? }
```
- **Units:** 1 unit = one block = one metre. Rotation in degrees, Euler applied Z * Y * X about the node pivot (the Blockbench / RigSpec / Model Studio L2 convention, so poses agree across the studio).
- **Time:** integer ticks at the canonical 20 Hz. Keys may sit on fractional ticks; exporters resample (Minecraft 1 tick, Hytale fps, glTF seconds).
- **Rig nodes** (one concept for creature bones, gun parts and vehicle parts): `{ name, parent, kind, pivot, rest?, hinge?, wheel?, seat?, proxy? }`. Kinds: `bone`, `part`, `socket`, `hinge {axis, min, max}`, `wheel {axle, radius, steer?}`, `seat`, `emitter`. Names `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}$` (RigSpec's BONE_RE), one root. `proxy` is an optional preview box (size, offset, colour) for the simulator; real geometry comes from Model Studio or the game binding.
- **Clips:** `{ name, length (ticks), loop: once | loop | hold | pingpong, tracks[] }`.

### Track kinds (five)
| Kind | Fields | Neutral meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `transform` | node, channel pos/rot/scale, `keys[{t, v, ease}]` or `wave{amp, offset, cycles, phase}` | node offset from rest; waves are the parametric gait primitive |
| `particle` | node, at, duration (0 = burst), `effect` (catalog ref `effect:<id>`) or inline emitter (shape, burst/rate, lifetime, speed, spread, gravity, size, colour ramp, sprite), seed | emitter attached to a node |
| `sound` | at, `sound` (catalog `sound:<id>` or namespaced key), gain, pitch, node? | cue at a tick |
| `material` | node, channel emissive / opacity / tint / frame / brightness, keys (step or linear) | light flash, glow, texture frame |
| `event` | at, name, optional `attach {child, socket}` / `detach {child}` | named marker; machine input; attach = reparent (character into a seat) |

Ease: `linear`, `step`, `in`, `out`, `inout`, `smooth` (smoothstep, = RigSpec "smooth").

## 2. State machines
`Machine { name, initial, vars[{name, init, min, max}], states[{name, clip?, onEnter[], after?{to, ticks?}}], transitions[{from | "*", on, to, guard?, minTicks?}] }`. Actions: `set`, `add` (clamped to the var range), `emit` (raise an event this tick). Guards compare one integer var (`lt le eq ne ge gt`). `after` without ticks = the end of a `once` clip.

Example gun: idle -(fire, ammo > 0)-> fire (onEnter ammo -1; after -> idle); idle -(fire, ammo = 0)-> dry; * -(reload, ammo < 6)-> reload (after -> idle, onEnter ammo = 6). Door: closed -(toggle)-> opening (after -> open) -(toggle)-> closing (after -> closed); `minTicks` stops spam.

Triggers come from outside: the ability graph (`trigger_motion` in a later step), a click on the prop, a command, or the studio's simulation controls.

## 3. Sampler and determinism
- `sample(spec, clip, tick) -> Pose` (per node pos/rot/scale + material values) is PURE: no clock, no `Math.random`, results rounded to 1e-4 and -0 removed, so golden tests are byte-stable.
- `cues(spec, clip, from, to)` returns the sound / particle-start / event cues in the half-open window (from, to], so a step of N ticks never fires a cue twice or skips one, including across loop wraps.
- Particles are analytic: particle i of an emitter has a seeded (mulberry32(seed, i)) direction, speed and lifetime; its position at age a is `origin + v a + g a^2 / 2`. Any frame can be rendered without integrating the ones before it (scrubbing and contact sheets are exact).
- `runMachine(spec, machine, inputs, ticks)`: inside one tick, inputs apply in array order, then `emit`s, then `after`; at most 8 transitions per tick (a cycle is cut and reported); the new state's clip starts at tick 0 of the transition tick. Same inputs = same frames, always.

## 4. Clock / simulation contract with the viewport
There is ONE playback clock: the Model Studio timeline clock (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/editor/timeline/clock.ts`: play, pause, scrub, loop, speed, `clockTick(dt)`; no timers inside). The L1 viewport feeds it elapsed seconds from its own `requestAnimationFrame`; the motion simulation steps every whole tick crossed (`ticksCrossed(prev, next)`, 20 per second) and the renderer draws `sample()` at the fractional tick for smooth playback. ONE persisted animation model: MotionSpec. ModelDoc v1 (the L2 editor document) stores the creature's transform tracks and clip events, a projection that converts losslessly both ways (`fromLegacyClipFull` / `toLegacyClip`); the editor's extension kinds (sound cue, particle burst, light, material, state) have their home in the MotionSpec, and the editor's transform sampler is held equal to `sample()` by a parity test. three.js maps Pose onto object transforms; Rapier only for a vehicle dynamics preview, never exported truth.

## 5. Exporter / adapter contract
Each adapter declares a `motion` capability in its AssetProfile:
```
MotionCapability { tickRate, trackKinds: {transform|particle|sound|material|event: native|approx|none},
  nodeKinds[], materialChannels[], attach: boolean, interpolation: "linear-segments"|"keyframes"|"none",
  caps: { nodes, clips, tracks, keysPerTrack, durationTicks, particlesPerTick, particlesPerClip,
          liveEntities, soundsPerClip, machines, states }, delivery, maturity }
```
`lower(spec, capability, ctx) -> { ok, program | null, warnings[], dropped[{path, reason}] }`. Unsupported tracks degrade with an explicit `dropped` row; nothing is silently lost. `validateMotion(spec, caps)` gives structured issues `{path, code, severity, message}` against the profile caps before any lowering.

**Minecraft (first slice):** each rig part = one `item_display` or `block_display` at the instance origin (no passenger chains); the lowering bakes the node hierarchy into each part's world transform per tick and emits interpolation SEGMENTS `{start, duration, translation, leftRotation, scale}` (V: Paper `setTransformation`, `setInterpolationDelay`, `setInterpolationDuration`; changes in one tick count as one). Client interpolation is linear between segments (U), so easing is chained short segments within an error budget (0.01 block, 1 degree), max 90 degrees per segment; `step` = duration 0. Sound cues play by key at their tick (`sound:<id>` resolved through the Sound Library), particle tracks map to data-free vanilla particles within the designer BUDGET (512 per activation, 64 per burst), `material.brightness` lowers to display brightness, other material channels and `attach` are dropped with reasons. Clicks reach the machine through an `interaction` entity. Parts are non-persistent (gone on restart; nothing leaks into worlds).

## 6. Catalog presets
Presets are MotionSpecs with kinds `motion` (clips, rigs, machines: gun_fire, gun_reload, door_hinge, creature gait) and `effect` (particle/sound/light bundles: muzzle_flash, explosion, fire, smoke, water_splash). Each entry carries per-game support (computed by dry-running every adapter's `lower`), provenance `cyrus-authored`, licence `nxeon-original`, parameters with ranges. The catalog v2 `CATALOG_KINDS` gets `motion`/`effect` only after the owner's gating decision (section 7), so v0 presets live in `lib/cyrus/motion/presets` with the same entry shape.

## 7. Plan-tier gating proposal (owner decides)
| Option | Presets + AI composition | Custom motion editing (timeline) | Effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (recommended) | every paid plan, like designer components (not asset generation) | Model plan (All) | every paid plan |
| B | Saka+ | All | Saka+ |
| C | everything All | All | All |
Keep / install / export never gated (unchanged rule).

## 8. Studio integration
- **Texture Studio:** `material.frame` drives animated textures (`.mcmeta` frametime/frames, V) and decal swaps; `emissive` previews glow; onion skin shows neighbouring ticks.
- **Sound Studio:** `sound` cues reference library ids; the timeline draws the waveform under the cue lane with markers at ticks; "snap to transient" moves a cue to the nearest onset (peaks from the sound library); cue-to-visual error on Minecraft is about 1 tick plus jitter (U), so cues snap to whole ticks.
- **Model Studio:** L1 viewport owns the clock; L2 timeline edits tracks; rig nodes are its bones plus socket/hinge/wheel/seat metadata.

## 9. AI generation strategy
1. **Pick a preset** (`{ use: "motion:gun_reload", params: { magDrop: 0.4 } }`) - cheapest and most reliable.
2. **Parametric generators** with typed knobs: gait (archetype biped/quadruped/flyer, stride, bob, swing, phase), hinge (axis, angle, ticks, ease, bounce), recoil (kick, return ticks), slide cycle, wheel spin (later).
3. **Full MotionSpec** only for simple mechanical motion; the validator's issues go back for one repair round.
4. **Human fix** in the timeline (nudge keys, snap cues to the waveform); every edit is a revision.
Claude emits JSON only (no code); a mod file wraps it as a design (`assets/designs/<id>.json`, `"kind": "motion"`) with a game binding. Not reliable and not promised: mocap-quality humans, free-form creature acting, frame-accurate audio sync by ear.

## 10. Per-game roadmap
| Game | Lowering | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Minecraft Java | display-entity segments, vanilla particles, sound keys, item model states; creature clips to BetterModel `.bbmodel` (26.x) | slice 1 now (gun + door) |
   200 src/ext.js
   245 src/kit.css
   140 src/kit.js
    95 src/mo.css
    39 src/mo.js
   228 src/motion.html
   194 src/ms.css
    43 src/ms.js
    99 src/presets.html
    97 src/v2.css
  1380 total

## Cyrus designer studio UI (2026-10-10, branch `feature/cyrus-r27-designer-ui`, NOT deployed, flags OFF)

The screens where a person changes by hand what Cyrus designed: the **Item Designer**, the **Menu + Quest designer**, the **Boss + encounter designer** and the **Motion panel** (timeline, preview, preset browser). They follow the v2 / v4 mockups (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v2/`, `v4-motion/`) closely; **the owner has not reviewed those mockups yet**, so expect change requests. The boss screen has no mockup: it reuses the Item Designer's anatomy.

**Where.** Full pages in the studio shell: `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/items` (`?item=`), `/studio/menus` (`?tab=quests`, `?menu=`, `?quest=`), `/studio/bosses` (`?boss=`), `/studio/motion` (`?motion=`, `?view=presets`). The top bar's switch is Items / Menus / Quests / Bosses (Motion sits in the Texture / Sound / Model / Motion switch, as in the v4 mockup).

**Gates (all server side, fail closed).** 404 unless `CYRUS_DESIGNER=1` (the existing designer switch, off), then the studios gate (`cyrus_studios_enabled` or a preview account, plus ownership of the build). Every API answers 404 to anyone else (`lib/cyrus/designer/studio/deps.ts` `designerViewer`). Designers are **not plan-gated**; the asset chips (item model texture, custom sounds) show the asset gate's own decision (texture: All models, sound: Saka+, Free / Katara: none) and link to the Texture / Sound Studio, whose APIs refuse edits anyway. Rate limits per person: read 120/min, check 240/min, simulate 240/min, save 30/min, draft 60/min.

**API** (`/api/cyrus/designer/v1`, handlers in `lib/cyrus/designer/studio/http.ts`, framework-free, tested with fakes):
- `GET /projects?root=<rootBuildId>`: the mod's designs (newest `design` asset row per key; rows written by a Texture / Sound Studio candidate build are ignored), their history, the analysis of the saved designs, the limits, the plan view for the asset chips, the mod's asset keys and the person's draft.
- `POST /projects/:id/check { files }`: validate + compile the working copy against the saved designs (no write).
- `POST /projects/:id/revisions { files, expectedHeadId }`: save. The whole mod must validate (`validateGameplay`: items, menus, quests, bosses, encounters, HUDs, motions + the cross-file checks) and compile (`compileMod`); then a NEW revision (kind `edited`, status `pending`: nothing was built) whose manifest replaces the changed `assets/designs/<id>.json` entries, plus one new `design` asset row per changed design (origin `edited`, provenance: the spec, compile hash, config_version, configOnly, the Java files that change, the row it was based on). Refused: a stale head (409), invalid / not compiling (422 with the analysis), nothing changed (400), and any change to the SET of design files (add / remove / rename = a change build).
- `PUT|DELETE /projects/:id/draft`: the autosaved working copy, one per project and person, in the existing `CyrusModelDraft` table under the asset key `designer` (no new table; the same additive migration the Model Studio editor already needs). Autosave: 5 s idle, at most 30 s (the Model Studio schedule). A draft is restored on open unless the mod moved on since (then it is offered for discarding). `CYRUS_DESIGNER_DRAFTS=memory` keeps drafts in the process (devhost / tests only, never production).
- `POST /projects/:id/simulate`: the reference simulators on the working copy (valid designs only): `item` (the ability simulator on a fixed sample world: you at the origin, zombies / skeleton / husk at 6.5-18.4 blocks, a cow at 4; steps hit / kill / click / sneak click / charge N ticks / wait / consume / projectile / join / die; the buttons come from the item's triggers), `menu` (Try it: a sample player with 9 emeralds, level 7, no Vault, 6 free slots and the menu's permissions clicks through the fixed protocol room -> pay -> take -> give), `quests` (player events derived from the active steps; +24 h), `boss` (the fight simulator: hits of 10 / 25 % health, waits, a second player, leaving the arena).
- `POST /projects/:id/plan { text, files }`: `planDesignEdit`, the deterministic settings-only recogniser. A recognised request is applied in the editor as value edits (no model call, nothing sent anywhere); the person still reviews and saves. Anything else says "needs a change build", shows the token estimate and copies the request for the mod's chat (the designer does not start builds).

**Pure core** (`lib/cyrus/designer/studio/`): `edit.ts` (client-safe: the config-path setter, a port of `params.ts setInDesign` + `gameplay/params.ts` incl. the boss pointers; a test checks it agrees with `applyGameplayEdits` for every fixture parameter; structural helpers: add / remove action, add condition, add ability, the JSON view), `analyze.ts` (validators, the static budgets `budgetOf` / `bossBudgetOf`, the parameters `modParams`, two compiles and `diffCompiled`: "config.yml only, config_version 1 -> 2" vs the Java files a structural edit rebuilds; the motion designs' Minecraft fit: caps, what the lowering leaves out, the lowered program's size), `sim.ts` (scripts -> simulator events), `service.ts` (deps injected: the studios' store, the build chain, the plan lookup, the draft store). No new imports of Nxeon internals under `lib/cyrus` (the seam test passes); everything reaches Nxeon through `lib/cyrus/studios/deps.ts`.

**UI** (`components/cyrus/designers/`): `shared.tsx` (`useDesigner`: the working copy, the debounced server check, autosave, save, discard; meters, steppers, issue rows, the pending bar), `ItemDesigner.tsx`, `MenuQuestDesigner.tsx`, `BossDesigner.tsx`, `MotionStudio.tsx`, `designers.css` (dz-* / mo-* on the studios' tokens; one accent, cyan only for "now", real light mode), `pixel-icons.ts` (the mockups' **placeholder** pixel icons for vanilla items, labelled as such; an item whose model is one of the mod's textures shows that real texture), `icons.tsx`. Every value field is the same `config.yml` parameter in the graph and in the Parameters tab (path, range, the old value struck through); the server check is the only judge (budget meters and error rows use the validator's own codes, e.g. `budget_particles`, `economy_needs_vault`). Phones (< 760 px container): a read-only summary with Approve / Reject when an autosaved draft is waiting (Approve saves it as a revision, Reject discards it). The Motion panel runs the motion core in the browser (the preset built from its knobs, `simulate`, the software `renderFrame`); keyframes of a preset come from its knobs, so they are read-only here (custom specs: Model Studio's timeline).

**Honest limits.** Saved designer revisions stay in Cyrus: the build service starts a change build from the base build's own source, so **a saved designer edit does not reach a server yet** (the pending bar says so); wiring "builds start from the studio's designs" is an open engineering item (the same gap as Model Studio editor saves). Nothing here was verified in a real game client; the simulators are logic only (no physics, ray tracing, protection plugins, pathfinding or client). Icons are placeholders (owner question: the production icon source).
EOF
echo ok

# X: Cyrus designer studio UIs (r27, 2026-10-10/11)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r27-designer-ui` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r27`, from `feature/cyrus-r2` at 702cd62d86, which already holds the boss/encounter + HUD designers and the motion kind). NOT deployed, NOT merged, flags OFF. **The owner has not reviewed the v2 / v4 mockups these screens follow: expect change requests.**

## What was built
1. **Item Designer** (`/studio/items`): item header (name in its MC colour, rarity, glint, id, base, lore, stats), plan-gated asset chips (texture: All models, sound: Saka+; links to the studios), display-context preview (the shipped In-game renderer: hotbar, dropped, first / third person, frame, head), the When -> Only if -> Do ability graph (trigger fields, re-entry guard, cooldown, charges, conditions, nested query / delayed / branch containers, config paths per block), the 5 budget meters (the validator's `budgetOf`) and the validator's real error codes, Parameters (config path, range, old value struck through), "config.yml only, config_version 1 -> 2, N files unchanged" vs the Java files a structural edit rebuilds, the Simulator tab (the reference simulator on a sample world, timeline + log), Checks (the 8 DESIGN_CHECKS rows, compile, real client = not run, structure vs settings), JSON view, add action / condition / ability, remove block, the dock (settings-only requests via `planDesignEdit` applied in the editor, no model call; anything else: token estimate + "needs a change build").
2. **Menu + Quest designer** (`/studio/menus`, `?tab=quests`): slot grid (buttons, list slots, nav, costs, permissions), slot inspector (on-click protocol, cost / action chips, config values, permission, `economy_needs_vault`), Try it (sample player through the real CostCharger order), the owner-editable shop list (amount / price), checks per menu; quest chain, step flow (objectives with editable counts, branches, rewards), progress simulator with player events, stored-progress and active-quest meters, quest check rows.
3. **Boss + encounter designer** (`/studio/bosses`; no mockup exists, it reuses the item designer's anatomy): header (stats editable, immunities, boss bar), phase ladder on the health bar (thresholds, intervals, attack weights, phase-start actions), the selected attack (targets, range, cooldown, telegraph, per-attack budget incl. summons), arena (top-down to scale), Parameters, Fight simulator (the reference BossFight), checks; encounter waves.
4. **Motion panel** (`/studio/motion`, studio switch Texture / Sound / Model / Motion): rig tree, state machine + vars, scripted events, the browser-run motion core (preset built from its knobs, `simulate`, software `renderFrame`), transport + timeline (state band, keys where played, cue lanes, scrubbing), Knobs (preset params = the edit), Export (Minecraft caps, lowered program, what is left out), Checks; preset browser with live posters and "Use for <motion>"; phone read-only card.

Backend: `lib/cyrus/designer/studio/` (edit / analyze / sim / service / http / deps) + `/api/cyrus/designer/v1/**`; save = a NEW `edited` revision (status pending) + one design row per changed design; autosave drafts in `CyrusModelDraft` (key `designer`). Details: docs "Cyrus designer studio UI".

## Ran vs not run
- RAN: `test/cyrus-designer-studio.test.ts` (RESULT_TESTS) incl. the client edit port == `applyGameplayEdits` for every fixture parameter, analysis codes, simulators, service save / stale / invalid / drafts, handlers 404 without a viewer; host-seam ratchet; `tsc` clean; full Cyrus suite RESULT_SUITE.
- RAN: Playwright on node-2 against `devhost dev` with fixtures (`scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` + `scripts/cyrus/designer-fixtures.ts`), RESULT_SHOTS screenshots `cyrus-designs/impl-shots/designer-*.png`, looked at and fixed (Tailwind `.fixed` collision, crumb overflow, header wrap, double-counted errors, verdict badge). Real API round trips: autosave -> draft restored on reopen, settings-only plan, simulators.
- NOT RUN: any real game client; any paid model call (none exist in this UI); a production build (`next build`); eslint over the whole app.

## Known gaps (honest)
- **A saved designer revision does not reach a server yet**: change builds start from the base build's own source. Needs the build request to carry the studio's designs.
- Item icons are labelled placeholders (open owner question); a mod's own texture shows when it has one.
- Structural editing is basic (add action from templates, add condition, add ability, remove, JSON view); no drag-and-drop, no trigger-kind switcher.
- node-2's agent slice OOM-killed the dev server several times while other agents' dev servers ran; screenshots were taken in batches.
